materials.title: A Day in Ben's Life
contentText:
Ben is twelve years old. He lives in London.

On Monday, Ben gets up at seven o'clock. In the morning, he has breakfast at home. He goes to school at half past seven.

At school, Ben has lunch at twelve o'clock. In the afternoon, he plays football with his friends.

In the evening, Ben does his homework at six o'clock. He watches TV at eight o'clock. He goes to bed at half past nine.

materials.title: Prepositions for Time — at, in, on
contentText:
English uses three small words to say when something happens: at, in, and on. Each one goes with a different type of time expression — they are not interchangeable.

Use at with clock times: at seven o'clock, at half past nine.
Use in with parts of the day (morning, afternoon, evening) and seasons: in the morning, in winter.
Use on with days of the week: on Monday, on Friday.

Watch out: German am looks like "at the" in English, but the English rule for parts of the day is in, not at. So am Morgen = in the morning (not "at the morning"). German am Montag = on Monday (not "at Monday"). German um 7 Uhr = at 7 o'clock.
at half past nine — at school — on Friday — in the evening
